To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the first self-assembled monolyer functionalized half-metallic oxide is presented, which can be used as a tunneling barrier in spintronic nanodevices.
the first self-assembled monlayer (SAM) of alkylphonic acids over the half-metallic oxide (La,SrMnO3) manganites has been realized.
self-assembled monolyaers of alkylphophonic acids are grafted on LSMO surface and act as tunnel barriers in spintronic devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication, the characterization and the integration into nanodevices of self-assembled monolyers over a half metallic oxide.
the fabrication of self-assembled monomolecular layers of phosphonic acid derivatives on the half-metallic oxide (La,Sr)(MnO3) manganites.
the fabrication and characterization of molecular spintronic devices based on self-assembled monomolecular layers of alkylphoshponic acids on the surface of half-metallic mangesium oxide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the grafting of SAMs over the LSMO surface thin film is a feasible approach for the integration of organic materials into spintronic devices.
the self-assembled monolyer-functionalization of half-metallic oxides is a key step for the integration of organic materials in future spintronic devices.
we have successfully demonstrated for the first time that SAMs can be functionalized over a LSMO half-metal, opening the door to molecular spintronics and molecular spin devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a simple and robust method to functionalize the half-metallic oxide (La,Sr)(Mn)O(3) (LSMO) surface with alkylphosphonates, thus paving the way for molecular engineering of organic/organic spintrionic devices based on LSMO electrodes.
we are reporting the first self-assembled monolyayer (SAM)-functionalized half-metallic LSMO thin films for spintronic devices.

we have demonstrated that alkylphosphonates can form ordered self-assemblies on the half-metallic molybdenum oxide (La,Sr)manganite (LSM) and we have shown that these SAMs act as tunnel barriers in nanodeviced.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SAMs are a promising material for spintronics.
the grafting of SAMs on half-metallic molybdenum oxide is possible, and that these SAMs can be integrated in molecular/organic spintronics devices.
SAMs are promising candidates for the molecular engineering of spintronics devices.
